Phantom approval removal is a useful startup-governance fix, but the selected detached-work object exposes a broader terminal-truth boundary for delegated work.
Host-bound gateway credentials define a clear trust boundary, but the selected attachment-owned MCP authority object spans the richer runtime-refresh lifecycle.

Mandatory user interaction becoming non-bypassable is a strong authority rule, but the selected detached-work object more directly tests whether delegated execution is represented truthfully at workflow completion.
Automatic continuation after transport failure improves liveness, but the selected object addresses the more fundamental terminal-truth contract for delegated work.
Explicit partial status at maxTurns improves completion semantics, but the selected detached-node failure propagation mechanism is the stronger workflow-level terminal-truth question.
Worktree launch isolation is architecturally useful, but the selected MCP permission-profile object provides a sharper authority-ownership boundary across runtime refresh.
Malformed poll retry improves runner resilience, but the selected RunConfig isolation mechanism addresses reusable invocation-state contamination more directly.

Typed MCP result preservation improves result fidelity, but the selected object has a more direct mutable-state safety and cross-invocation isolation mechanism.

Selected because mutation-specific copies keep live HTTP clients shared by reference while isolating mutable RunConfig containers, preventing callback mutations from leaking caller-owned state into later invocations.
Credential redaction in debug logs tightens observability safety, but the selected object addresses the deeper runtime-state isolation boundary.
Unary nested AgentTool execution ensures complete tool results, but the selected detached-work mechanism is the stronger workflow-level terminal-truth question.
